blindSummary:
The most concentrated wave of mob violence against transgender women in this country: ten attacks on 45 victim-survivors in one of its cities between March and July 2026. Attackers punched, kicked, threw stones, glass bottles and firecrackers, and stripped some victims naked. Groups of 10-20 men filmed the assaults for social media under an anti-LGBT vigilante handle that branded the city as cleaned of LGBT people. No alleged perpetrator has been publicly identified, arrested or prosecuted; a trans-rights activist accompanying women who filed police reports said officers "accepted the case but worked on it half-heartedly." Additionally, 75 people were detained at a resort-area villa raid (June 2025) that violated no law. Activists attribute the violence to a 2025 national regulation classifying "LGBT culture" as a non-military threat, stating "people feel able to commit violence arbitrarily because they believe the state has legitimised that violence."

This is well below the country-wide average. Unlike the capital jurisdiction, where a discriminatory raid on 56 people prompted immediate demands from an international human-rights organisation and the detainees lacked legal charges, this wave shows patterned vigilante violence with total state inaction and explicit anti-trans branding over four months.
